text:
ConocoPhillips climbed 4.2% today to $136.19, driven by a sharp rise in crude oil prices following U.S. military strikes against Iran that pushed global crude toward $90 per barrel. Oil majors like ConocoPhillips benefit directly when prices rise—higher crude prices improve the margins on both their exploration and refining operations. The stock's broader two-week rally of 5% tracks the same oil price movement, which has climbed as Middle East tensions have escalated.

The company also stands to benefit indirectly from the emerging Venezuelan oil deal announced over the weekend, which signals a potential increase in long-term crude supply access for U.S. firms. While the deal's actual impact remains uncertain, the headline signal of expanded U.S. oil production partnerships helped sustain upward momentum in the sector heading into today's session.
